newFindingAppearances.key: Important — skills/super-code/coordinator.js:432: The verification guard compares verified.sourceTree only against the current event's observed record. A normal verification-only reply omits observed, so !observed makes the guard true even if that exact source tree and command/configuration already has a retained live/fail observation. Concrete history: the existing fixture establishes baseline a/pass, A source b/fail and owner bd-A; append a reply with evidence [b/live/pass] and an association containing verification:0 but no observed/runBaseline. The reducer retains the original b/fail comparison, sets state=verified, and records no contradiction gap. This is the same immutable tested source as the recorded failure, not evidence of a repaired source; the contradictory outcomes need reconciliation. Callers explicitly retire the qualifier on this verified state, so the open repair can disappear. Compare the verification source/outcome against retained linked observations (and other associated outcomes), preserve ownership/open state with a contradiction gap when they conflict, and add a deterministic fixture for verification-only contradiction after durable re-entry. If repeat measurements are intentionally reconciled, require explicit supported reconciliation rather than silently accepting the later pass. The within-one-event baseline/observed same-tree guard does not cover this durable-history path.

newFindingAppearances.key: skills/super-code/coordinator.js:1511 — Resumed records whose tracker beads are partly open enter closeAlreadyMerged, which calls confirmClosure. That function calls clearPendingClosure at line 1246; noteRecovery/readRecovery remove the pending-closure obligation immediately, before the buffered ledger:<id> append is confirmed. closeAlreadyMerged then settles completed at line 1270. If ledger:<id> and its retry return null (or report appended:false), drainLedger merely drains the chain and the run returns completed with the recovery obligation absent. The new confirmation-aware Resume fast path at lines 724–731 only protects records observed fully closed at the first observation. This violates the brief's requirement to drain confirmed closure/updated obligation records before treating recovery as settled, and the report's claim that in-memory obligations change only after confirmed append. Route partial-close completion through the same confirmed durable transaction, retaining the original record and a scoped recovery-held result on failed append. Add a targeted fixture with an initially open associated bead, successful close/check, and failed ledger:<id> append/retry; assert recovery remains unresolved and a subsequent restart observes facts rather than blindly repeating closure.

newFindingAppearances.key: skills/super-auto/scripts/report-status:107 — Discover and archive the actual direct-review package `final-review-ID.md.diff`. The collector discovers only `prefix+'.diff'`, while the real Workflow producer at skills/super-code/coordinator.js:2757 invokes review-package with `${reviewPath}.diff` and reviewPath is `final-review-ID.md`. A settled direct review can therefore return collection complete without preserving its input diff, allowing cleanup to destroy that source. The same incorrect suffix in hasBundle (:93) can classify a null/no-work return with a leftover actual direct package as artifact-free. Update discovery and null bundle detection to match the producer, and use producer-shaped .md.diff fixtures (tests/super-auto/test-scripts.sh:352 currently invents the shorter .diff filename). Retain byte-for-byte/idempotent archive assertions for that real filename.

newFindingAppearances.key: `skills/super-code/coordinator.js:195-198` — Merge retry results per independent source instead of selecting/spreading whole dispatch objects. For example, the first Finish dispatch can return unavailable ledger transport but a successful `landed` list and complete `reviewBase`/`reviewHead`. If the retry returns valid ledger transport but `landedError` and `reviewError`, line 195 returns only the retry: the successful landing evidence and captured revision pair disappear. Final review then becomes unavailable despite the previously captured immutable source, and metrics loses supported Git evidence. If both ledger transports are unavailable, line 198 can instead retain first.landed alongside retry.landedError; the metrics caller rejects that successful list because of the error. This contradicts the explicit partial-results/independent-source retention contract. Retain each successful Git observation and each coherent complete review pair independently of ledger status, keep failed attempts as qualified gaps, and avoid combining half revision pairs. Add targeted replay cases with success/failure alternating independently across the three sources.

Thus implement, task review, verification-close, fix, seam/check-fix review, merge, plan, triage, check-evidence and non-final assembly throw before producing output, including current ledgers with valid IDs. Preserve strict live startup and separate internal builder initialization from operational Resume/Launch; forward genuine selected-Launch IDs consistently and retain identity-free legacy non-review rendering without minting or fabricating tokens. Keep persisted-ID review gates strict. Verify the actual ordinary dispatch suite plus both startup/replay checks on the integrated fix.

The report itself acknowledges the confirmed caller failure. Parent direction to leave dispatch-text untouched bounds the implementation scope; it does not waive the global preservation requirement or make the captured tree safe to integrate. The separate `startup-builder-seam-assessment-r1.md` recommends a follow-on seam repair but supplies neither delivered code nor passing verification. A genuine ID handoff repairs current-ID ledgers only; legacy identity-free non-review builder loading also needs separation from operational startup. Do not weaken live Resume validation, add synthetic identities, or treat a CLI override as persisted identity.
